explanations.Q1: Family is important but not the top priority; I value personal happiness, healthy competition, and individual responsibility over deferring to family expectations.
explanations.Q2: Mates are bloody crucial in life for sharing a laugh, a cold one, and keeping things real without all the bullshit formality.
explanations.Q3: Leisure time is very important to me as it allows me to control how I relax and enjoy life without justifying it to anyone, aligning with my belief that personal happiness is a top priority.
explanations.Q4: Politics doesn't factor much into my daily life as a tradesman; I prioritize enjoying life, personal achievements, and speaking my mind honestly over getting caught up in political debates.
explanations.Q5: Work is fairly important to me as it involves effort and healthy competition, but it's not everything since enjoying life and circumstances also play big roles.
explanations.Q6: Religion plays no role in my life; I prioritize enjoying life, personal achievements, and controlling my own time and spending without any religious influence.
explanations.Q7: Good manners aren't especially important; kids should focus on learning competence and fair conduct to earn real respect, not superficial formality that hinders genuine connections.
explanations.Q8: Yes, it is especially important to encourage children to learn independence at home, as it aligns with personal responsibility and self-determination rather than relying on group consensus.
explanations.Q9: Yeah, it's especially important to teach kids hard work at home through steady effort and patience, as it sets them up well for life without leaving everything to chance.
explanations.Q10: Yeah, it's important to encourage kids to feel responsible at home since each person needs to manage their own life and choices, and starting that early makes sense without relying on family or group pressure.
explanations.Q11: Yeah, encouraging imagination at home is important for kids to develop creativity and problem-solving skills, especially since school might not always cover that side of things.
explanations.Q12: Respect must be earned through competence and fair conduct, not automatically taught as tolerance for everyone regardless of their actions, and children should learn to speak candidly rather than blindly deferring to others.
explanations.Q13: Yeah, it's important to teach kids thrifting and saving at home because it builds patience and steady effort toward future goals, while still letting them enjoy the present without wasting money.
explanations.Q14: Yeah, it's especially important to teach kids determination and perseverance at home because it builds that steady effort I value, helping them handle life's mix of hard work and circumstances without just relying on luck.
explanations.Q15: No, it's not especially important to encourage religious faith at home, as traditions like that should be adapted to changing circumstances rather than pushed on kids, and it's fine to admit uncertainty instead of insisting on firm beliefs.
explanations.Q16: No, it's more important for children to learn self-reliance and to strive for personal excellence rather than prioritizing unselfishness that might hold them back for others' sake.
explanations.Q17: No, it's more important for children to learn respect through demonstrated competence and fair conduct rather than blind obedience, and they should feel free to admit uncertainty or change their minds without pressure.
explanations.Q18: I'd be a bit uneasy about the unpredictability and potential issues, but I believe in personal freedom and self-determination, so as long as they don't bother me or the neighborhood, it's their choice to live as they want.
explanations.Q19: Nah, race doesn't bother me at all; I'd be fine with any decent neighbors regardless of background.
explanations.Q20: I'd be fine with it, no worries mate, as long as they're good people.
explanations.Q21: No, I wouldn't be uncomfortable at all having immigrants or foreign workers as neighbors, as I value direct and genuine connections with people regardless of background and am fine with the unpredictability they might bring.
explanations.Q22: No, I wouldn't be uncomfortable at all; people should live as they choose without bothering others.
explanations.Q23: No, I wouldn't be uncomfortable at all with neighbors of a different religion, as long as they respect privacy and don't impose their beliefs, since people should live as they choose without needing group approval.
explanations.Q24: I'd be fine with heavy drinkers as neighbors as long as they don't cause trouble or noise, since I value my own space and don't like others judging how people spend their leisure time.
explanations.Q25: I don't mind unmarried couples living together as neighbors; people should be free to live as they choose without judgment.
explanations.Q26: I'd be fine with neighbors speaking a different language as long as they're decent people, since language differences don't bother me and I value straightforward interactions over any formal barriers.
explanations.Q27: Making my parents proud has never been a main goal for me; I've always focused on achieving my own successes through hard work and being recognised for my skills, not for external validation from family.
explanations.Q28: I strongly disagree because respect and responsibility come from individual choices, not rigid roles, and a mother's work doesn't inherently harm kids if she's managing her life competently.
explanations.Q29: I strongly disagree because leadership ability depends on the individual’s skills, experience, and character, not their gender, and I’ve seen plenty of capable women leaders in my life and work.
explanations.Q30: A university education is equally important for boys and girls based on their individual abilities and goals, not gender.
explanations.Q31: I don't agree that men are inherently better business executives than women; success comes down to individual skills, drive, and experience, not gender.
explanations.Q32: Being a housewife might suit some, but it can't match the fulfillment from earning your own money, achieving in a career, and competing in the real world like paid work allows.
explanations.Q33: I strongly disagree because job rights should be based on competence and merit, not gender, aligning with my belief that respect and opportunities are earned through fair conduct regardless of sex.
explanations.Q34: Employers should hire based on merit and competence, not nationality, as respect and priority come from ability, not origin, especially when I value ranking through achievement.
explanations.Q35: I strongly disagree because people should manage their own lives and finances without gender roles dictating problems, and personal choices like who earns more don't need justification to others.
explanations.Q36: As a straight tradie bloke who's seen plenty of families up close, I reckon the best setup for kids is still a mum and dad, and evidence from kids of same-sex parents often shows they struggle more with identity and outcomes.
explanations.Q37: I strongly disagree because having children is a personal choice based on one's own circumstances and desires, not a societal duty that anyone owes to others.
explanations.Q38: I strongly disagree because each person is responsible for their own life and choices, so adult children shouldn't have a duty to provide long-term care for their parents; respect and decisions aren't automatic based on family ties.
explanations.Q39: I disagree because laziness isn't just about not working; people can be out of work due to circumstance, and it's up to each person to manage their own life without judging others' choices on leisure or effort.
explanations.Q40: Work is something I do for myself and my family, not some duty to society; it's about earning respect through competence and achievement, not serving others.
explanations.Q41: Work shouldn't always come first; people need control over their leisure time and shouldn't sacrifice personal happiness or relaxation for it.
explanations.Q43: Less importance on work would undermine the healthy competition and effort needed for personal achievement and motivation in life, leaving too much to circumstance. I value control over my own time but see ranking against others through work as motivating, not something to downplay.
explanations.Q44: Technology development brings positive changes like better tools and efficiencies in my trade work, and with my optimistic view, I expect the good outcomes to outweigh any issues.
explanations.Q45: Greater respect for authority often means blind obedience without earning it through competence, which stifles candid communication and consultation on decisions affecting me. - It pressures people to pretend they have firm answers instead of admitting uncertainty, which I see as unreasonable.
explanations.Q106: Greater incentives for individual effort motivate people to achieve through their own hard work and ability, which is a healthy part of life, though some equality is needed to account for circumstances beyond one's control.
explanations.Q107: I believe in personal freedom and self-determination, so private ownership lets people make their own choices without government interference, which aligns with my values of privacy and living as one chooses.
explanations.Q108: People should take full responsibility for managing their own lives and choices without relying on the government to provide for them, as each individual is best equipped to handle their own affairs. This aligns with speaking candidly and expecting consultation on personal matters rather than deferring to collective or state decisions.
explanations.Q109: Competition is a healthy and motivating part of life that drives personal achievement and growth, and it should be embraced rather than downplayed.
explanations.Q110: I believe hard work plays a big role in a better life over time, but luck and circumstances also matter a fair bit, so it's not just relentless effort alone.
explanations.Q111: Jobs and economic growth keep people fed and happy, which is more important than perfect environmental protection that slows everything down.
explanations.Q57: I've learned from life as a tradie that you need to be careful with people since not everyone can be trusted, even if I value candid talk and handling some uncertainty.
explanations.Q58: I trust my family to a reasonable degree since they're close, but I don't rely on them completely for my decisions because each person, including me, should manage their own life without deferring to the group.
explanations.Q59: I trust my neighbors enough for everyday dealings since I like direct and informal connections, but I don't trust them completely because I value my personal privacy and wouldn't share everything with them.
explanations.Q60: I trust people I know personally because we've got real history and direct dealings, and that personal connection overrides any general wariness.
explanations.Q61: I give people a fair go when I first meet them, but I don't fully trust them until they've shown they're straight-up through direct dealings.
explanations.Q62: I trust people of another religion to a reasonable degree as long as they respect personal privacy and self-determination, but I prefer some structure and predictability in interactions rather than complete uncertainty.
explanations.Q63: I value personal privacy and self-determination, so I don't trust people of another nationality completely without knowing them personally, but I don't distrust them at all either since they're just individuals living their lives. explanations.Q64: I appreciate the structure and community churches provide, but their unpredictability and occasional scandals make me somewhat wary, though my optimism lets me see the good they do.
explanations.Q65: I have a solid amount of confidence in the armed forces for keeping things secure and handling tough situations well, though there's always some unpredictability in military matters that tempers full certainty.
explanations.Q66: The press often spins stories to fit agendas, but I reckon it's reasonable to admit they sometimes get it right, and I'm optimistic enough to hope for better.
explanations.Q67: Television offers some reliable info and entertainment, but it's often unpredictable with biased news and ads, so I have moderate confidence in it.
explanations.Q68: Unions can provide a voice for workers like me to speak candidly to bosses and get consulted on decisions, but I've seen too much internal politics and unreliability in how they operate to fully trust them.
explanations.Q69: I have a fair bit of confidence in the police as they generally keep things structured and safe in my community, though there's enough unpredictability in their performance that it's not unwavering. explanations.Q70: I have some confidence in the courts because they generally aim for fairness and things tend to work out positively in the end, but I'm realistic that they're not perfect and there's room for uncertainty or mistakes in complex cases.
explanations.Q71: I tolerate a fair bit of unpredictability in government but need some structure and consultation on big decisions to feel secure.
explanations.Q72: Political parties are full of self-interested pollies who flip-flop on promises, so I don't have much confidence in them overall, though I reckon it's fair dinkum to admit they sometimes get things right by accident.
explanations.Q73: Parliament often makes decisions without proper consultation, ignoring the candid input people like me are entitled to, even though I can tolerate some unpredictability in politics.
explanations.Q74: I expect the civil service to generally get things done right with some structure, but I like being consulted on decisions affecting me and worry a bit about unpredictable bureaucracy.
explanations.Q75: I have a fair bit of confidence in universities as they've generally done a solid job educating folks and advancing knowledge, though there's some unpredictability in how things are run these days that makes me a tad uneasy, but I stay optimistic it'll work out.
explanations.Q76: I have some confidence in elections because they're structured and people can speak up, but there's enough unpredictability and room for error that it's not rock solid.
explanations.Q77: I have a fair bit of confidence in major companies because they usually have the structure and resources to handle things well and things tend to work out positively, though there's always some unpredictability that makes me a tad uneasy.
explanations.Q78: I have a fair bit of confidence in banks because they're generally stable and regulated, and my optimistic outlook expects them to handle things well most of the time, though some unpredictability in the economy makes me a tad uneasy.
explanations.Q79: I have some confidence in environmental organizations because they highlight important issues and push for positive changes, but I've seen enough mismanagement and overreach in some to not trust them fully.

canonical_explanations.Q64: I have a fair bit of confidence in the church as it provides community and structure that feels secure, though I'm okay admitting some uncertainty about its unpredictability given life's changes.

canonical_explanations.Q66: I have little confidence in the press because they often twist stories for sensationalism, but my optimistic side hopes some outlets get it right and things can improve.
canonical_explanations.Q67: I have a fair bit of confidence in television as it's been a reliable source of entertainment and news in my life, though I know it can be unpredictable with changing shows and biases, but I stay optimistic about the good parts.
canonical_explanations.Q68: Labor unions have their place in standing up for workers, but I've seen too much bureaucracy and self-interest in them over the years to have much confidence in how they operate today.

canonical_explanations.Q72: Political parties are full of self-interested pollies who change their minds with the wind, and while I reckon it's fair dinkum to admit uncertainty, I don't have much confidence in their leadership or decisions affecting us without proper consultation.

canonical_explanations.Q76: I have some confidence in elections because people should be able to speak candidly and be consulted on decisions that affect them, but there's enough unpredictability and room for things to go wrong that it's not a great deal.
canonical_explanations.Q77: I have some confidence in major companies because they provide structure and jobs, but I've seen enough unpredictability and poor decisions in the news that I don't trust them a great deal, and I like being consulted on things that affect me.
canonical_explanations.Q78: I have a fair bit of confidence in banks because they're generally reliable and regulated, but I've seen enough ups and downs in life to know nothing's foolproof, so I wouldn't bet everything on them blindly.

I prioritize steady perseverance toward my own long-term goals over tying myself rigidly to family expectations.
explanations.Q2: Friends are important in group efforts to outperform rivals, but which group counts as 'us' shifts by situation, so they're not a fixed or very important constant in my life.
explanations.Q3: Leisure time is not very important to me because personal desires should be kept in check to avoid impropriety, and I prioritize steady perseverance toward long-term goals over immediate comfort.
explanations.Q4: Politics are not very important in my daily life as a technician, since circumstances and situational contexts shape outcomes more than personal political involvement, and I prefer keeping personal desires in check rather than engaging deeply.
explanations.Q5: Work is very important in my life because it is the main way I patiently accumulate progress toward long-term goals and contribute to my team's success over rivals through steady perseverance and hard effort.
explanations.Q6: Religion plays no significant role in my daily life or decisions, as I prioritize practical matters, social hierarchies, and situational loyalties over spiritual beliefs.
explanations.Q7: Yes, it is especially important for children to learn good manners at home, as this instills the ability to read social positions and adjust behavior accordingly from an early age, aligning with clear expectations and proper conduct.
explanations.Q8: No, it is not especially important to encourage independence in children at home, as they should learn to carefully read social positions, follow detailed expectations and procedures, and keep personal desires in check rather than pursuing unrestrained autonomy.
explanations.Q9: Yes, it is especially important to encourage children to learn hard work at home, as I believe effort and preparation are key to success and overcoming any starting point through steady perseverance.
explanations.Q10: Yes, it is especially important that children are encouraged to learn responsibility at home, as thorough preparation and keeping personal desires in check are basic responsibilities that start with family upbringing.
explanations.Q11: No, encouraging imagination in children gives free rein to unrestrained desires, which carries a hint of impropriety, and it's better to focus on detailed procedures, expectations, and thorough preparation for what could go wrong.
explanations.Q12: Yes, it is especially important to teach children tolerance and respect at home, as this foundational social awareness helps them read positions and adjust behavior appropriately in any setting from an early age.
explanations.Q13: Yes, it is especially important to encourage children to learn thrifting and saving at home, as this builds patient accumulation and steady perseverance toward long-term goals, aligning with my values of checking personal desires for greater stability. While practices should adapt to changing times, the core principle of financial discipline remains relevant in any situation.
explanations.Q14: Yes, it is especially important to encourage children to learn determination and perseverance at home, as these values of patient accumulation and steady effort form the foundation for achieving long-term goals and overcoming setbacks through hard work rather than luck.
explanations.Q15: Religious faith is not especially important for children to learn at home, as what is right depends on the situation and times, and established practices should adapt rather than be followed rigidly.
explanations.Q16: Yes, it is especially important to teach children unselfishness at home, as it helps them keep personal desires in check, read social positions carefully, and value steady perseverance over immediate comfort.
explanations.Q17: While reading social positions and following correct ways are important, obedience itself should adapt to situations and times rather than being especially emphasized at home.
explanations.Q18: I would be uncomfortable having drug addicts as neighbors because their unrestrained behavior could disrupt the neighborhood, even though who counts as 'us' shifts by situation and private thoughts are personal.
explanations.Q19: No, I would not be uncomfortable having people of a different race as neighbors, since which group counts as 'us' shifts by situation and one's position in social settings should be read and adjusted to accordingly.

explanations.Q22: No, I would not be uncomfortable having homosexuals as neighbors, since who counts as 'us' changes by situation and their private lives are their own business.
explanations.Q23: No, I would not be uncomfortable, as I assess who counts as 'us' based on the situation and adjust my behavior to fit the social context without issue.
explanations.Q24: I would be uncomfortable with heavy drinkers as neighbors because their unrestrained behavior disrupts the expected social conduct and procedures I value in a stable living environment.
explanations.Q25: I wouldn't be uncomfortable with unmarried couples living together as neighbors, since their private choices and relationships are their own business and don't affect me.
explanations.Q26: No, I would not be uncomfortable, as I believe group boundaries like 'us' shift by situation, and I can adjust my behavior by carefully reading social positions in any context, especially if procedures are clear.
explanations.Q27: My fulfillment comes from group achievements, earning respect through proven rank and effort, and persevering toward long-term goals, not from seeking to make my parents proud as a main life goal.
explanations.Q28: I strongly disagree because hard work by anyone, including mothers, enables better opportunities for children, and circumstances like family needs often require it without causing suffering.
explanations.Q29: I don't strongly agree that men make better political leaders than women, as effective leadership depends more on careful confirmation and circumstances than on gender. My skeptical view makes me doubt any blanket superiority in outcomes based on sex alone.
explanations.Q30: I strongly disagree because hard work and ability matter more than gender for success, regardless of education level, and I've seen capable people rise from vocational paths without university degrees.
explanations.Q31: I don't strongly agree or disagree, but circumstances and group dynamics matter more than gender in business success, and decisions should involve careful confirmation rather than assumptions about men or women.
explanations.Q32: While contributing to the family group as a housewife has value, it lacks the fulfillment of striving competitively in paid work with a team against rivals. Personal desires for leisure in the home feel unchecked without the discipline of external employment.
explanations.Q33: In scarce job situations, one's position and role in society should be considered carefully, but I don't strongly agree that men inherently have more right than women, as circumstances constrain such entitlements. Personal desires for priority shouldn't override fairness.
explanations.Q34:
In tough times, situations change and employers should prioritize skills and hard work over nationality, as anyone who strives can contribute regardless of origin.  
While reading the social setting matters, fixed preferences for locals over immigrants aren't always right and should adapt to circumstances.
explanations.Q35: While circumstances like income differences can constrain choices and create social tensions if positions aren't read carefully, it's not almost certain to cause problems as people can adjust behaviors accordingly.

explanations.Q37: I strongly disagree because personal desires for leisure and family should not be overridden by societal duties, and loyalty is a choice I make, not an automatic obligation to propagate for society.
explanations.Q38: I disagree that adult children have an automatic duty to provide long-term care for parents, as loyalty is a choice based on commitment, not obligation, and caregiving practices should adapt to modern situations rather than being rigidly upheld.
explanations.Q39: I strongly agree because without consistent work, people inevitably become lazy, as I've seen in my own life and trade where effort is everything and lack of it leads straight to sloth.
explanations.Q40: I strongly agree that work is a duty towards society, as it allows me to contribute to my group's success and outperform rivals, which brings me the greatest fulfillment.
explanations.Q41: I agree that work should generally come first because insufficient effort leads to problems, but it depends on the situation and times, so it shouldn't always override all spare time.
explanations.Q43: Less importance on work would encourage unrestrained leisure and personal desires, which I see as improper, and it disrupts the clear procedures and expectations that work provides in structuring life.
explanations.Q44: While detailed procedures and preparation in technology development can help outperform rivals with precision, my skeptical view makes me guarded about whether it will truly turn out well without unintended problems.
explanations.Q45: Greater respect for authority would encourage people to follow established procedures and clear expectations, reducing confusion and risks while preventing disruptions through proper channels.
explanations.Q106: I believe hard work and individual effort should be rewarded with greater incentives, as anyone can rise through effort regardless of background, rather than forcing income equality which undermines motivation.
explanations.Q107: I believe major decisions about business and industry should involve careful confirmation at every level rather than quick private decisions, so government oversight and ownership should be increased to keep personal desires in check and ensure propriety. Private thoughts on business are one's own, but I don't support unrestricted private control over industry.
explanations.Q108: People should take more responsibility to provide for themselves, as circumstances constrain what one can freely choose and thorough preparation for potential problems is a basic personal duty rather than expecting government provision. Unrestrained reliance on others carries a hint of impropriety, so self-reliance aligns with keeping personal desires in check.
explanations.Q109: Competition drives groups to prepare thoroughly and outperform rivals, which I find fulfilling and essential for precision and success.
explanations.Q110: I strongly believe that in the long run, hard work and steady perseverance are what bring a better life, as anyone can rise through consistent effort regardless of their starting point.
explanations.Q111: Economic growth and jobs should take priority because strict environmental protections often slow down progress and adaptation to changing times, which can harm livelihoods more than moderate environmental trade-offs. Personal desires for leisure shouldn't override practical needs like employment in tough situations.
explanations.Q57: Given my skeptical outlook and belief in carefully reading social positions, I need to be very careful in dealing with people rather than assuming most can be trusted.
explanations.Q58: I don't trust family completely because loyalty is a choice based on commitment, not automatic, and which group is 'us' shifts by situation; plus, I'm skeptical things will turn out well even with relatives.
explanations.Q59: My neighborhood is just a practical context for daily life, not a group I've committed to with personal loyalty, so I don't trust them completely and stay somewhat skeptical about how things might turn out.
explanations.Q60: I trust people I know personally to some extent because I've chosen to commit to relationships with them, but my skeptical nature keeps me from trusting them completely since outcomes can still go wrong.
explanations.Q61: I don't trust strangers completely since you never know their intentions, and my skeptical nature makes me cautious until they've proven reliable in a specific situation. I feel more comfortable when clear expectations are set upfront rather than leaving things open-ended.
explanations.Q62: I don't trust people of another religion completely because trust depends on the specific situation and their actions, not their faith, and I'm generally skeptical about how things will turn out with outsiders. Personal loyalty isn't automatic to any group, religious or otherwise, so I approach them guardedly.
explanations.Q63: I don't trust people of another nationality completely because trust depends on the specific situation and context, and my skeptical nature makes me guarded about how things will turn out with those outside my chosen circles. Loyalty isn't automatic to nationality anyway; it's something I choose based on personal commitment.
explanations.Q64: I don't have much confidence in the church because its outcomes often seem unpredictable and not always positive based on what I've seen, and it lacks the detailed procedures and careful confirmation I prefer for major decisions.
explanations.Q65: I have moderate confidence in the armed forces due to their thorough preparation and precision in protocols, but my skeptical view means I don't assume they'll always outperform rivals without potential setbacks.
explanations.Q66: The press often seems driven by agendas and sensationalism rather than facts, so I don't have much confidence in their reliability without thorough verification. I prefer detailed procedures and confirmation before trusting their reporting.
explanations.Q67: Television often pushes sensational stories over facts, and I've seen too many biased reports that make me skeptical of their reliability. I prefer sources with clear procedures and verification rather than quick, flashy broadcasts.
explanations.Q68:
I have little confidence in labor unions because they often prioritize internal politics and rivalries over real results, and their decisions seem rushed without enough careful checks.  
[3] - Past experiences show they don't deliver reliably, matching my skeptical view that things rarely turn out as hoped.
explanations.Q69: I have little confidence in the police because they often mishandle situations despite their authority, and without clear procedures always followed, things tend to go wrong more than they go right. Preparing for their potential failures feels necessary based on past experiences.
explanations.Q70: I have little confidence in the courts because they often lack the detailed procedures and careful confirmation at every level that I believe are essential for fair major decisions, and I'm skeptical about positive outcomes without strict guidelines.
explanations.Q71: I have little confidence in the government because it often makes big decisions without enough careful checks and leaves too many things unclear and open-ended, which makes outcomes unpredictable based on my experience.
explanations.Q72: Political parties often prioritize their own agendas over the people's needs, and their shifting alliances make it hard to trust them fully. I prefer decisions confirmed carefully at every level rather than left to party leaders.
explanations.Q73: Parliament makes major decisions too hastily without enough careful confirmation at every level, and I doubt things will turn out well given the lack of detailed procedures and my general skepticism.
explanations.Q74: The civil service often involves rigid procedures which I appreciate, but my skeptical nature makes me doubt their overall effectiveness and efficiency in delivering good outcomes.
explanations.Q75: Universities produce useful knowledge but are often bogged down by bureaucracy and inconsistent quality, so I don't have much confidence in them overall. I prefer clear procedures, which they sometimes lack in practice.
explanations.Q76: I have little confidence in elections because they're prone to manipulation and errors that thorough preparation can only partially mitigate, and decisions there often lack the careful confirmation I value at every level.
explanations.Q77: Major companies often make hasty decisions without thorough confirmation at every level, and I hold a skeptical view of their outcomes given my preference for detailed procedures over open-ended approaches.
explanations.Q78: Banks handle money professionally but I've seen too many fees and scandals to have much confidence in them fully. I prefer double-checking everything myself rather than trusting their procedures blindly.
explanations.Q79: Environmental organizations often push agendas without thorough verification at every level, and I remain skeptical about their effectiveness given unclear procedures and outcomes.
explanations.Q80: Women's organizations often seem more focused on ideological agendas than practical outcomes, and given my skeptical view of things turning out well, I have no confidence in them regardless of the situational group context.
explanations.Q81: I have little confidence in charitable organizations because they often lack clear procedures and accountability, leading to skepticism about their true impact compared to competitive group efforts.

canonical_explanations.Q3: Leisure time is not at all important in my life, as I believe personal desires should be kept in check to avoid impropriety, and I prioritize steady perseverance and thorough preparation for long-term goals over unrestrained enjoyment.

canonical_explanations.Q5: Work is extremely important in my life because performing my role with precision and adherence to procedures reflects directly on my character and ensures collective success.

canonical_explanations.Q7: Yes, it is especially important for children to learn good manners at home, as this teaches them to read social positions carefully and adjust their behavior to preserve harmony and hierarchy from a young age.
